messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: tabsetPanel could use an active= parameter to specify the tab that should be (initially) active
parts:
For use in reactive UIs, it would be really handy if tabsetPanel took a parameter to specify the currently active tab.

I generate tabsets in a reactive function, and I want to make sure the selected tab doesn't change each time the reactive UI is generated, and if the old tab isn't available, I want to select the next appropriate one.

The tabset also feeds back to an input, which I can send back out each time the reactive ui updates.

I'll probably hack it in for myself for now.

-Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: tabsetPanel could use an active= parameter to specify the tab that should be (initially) active
parts:
What you're describing sounds like the opposite of what Alex was asking for in this thread. I'll describe both:

1) Alex was asking to be able to specify which tab in a tabset would be selected by default; that's the "selected" parameter on tabsetPanel

2) It sounds like you're asking to know which tab is currently selected; you specify the "id" parameter on tabsetPanel and use input$foo (for example, assuming id="foo") in your server.R.

messages.subject: Re: tabsetPanel could use an active= parameter to specify the tab that should be (initially) active
parts:
observe({
  if (identical(input$myPanel, "tab1")) {
    isImageAvailable <- ...   # presumably this would invoke accessing a reactive value or expr

    if (!isImageAvailable)
      updateTabsetPanel(session, "myPanel", selected="tab2")
  }
})

If you're not familiar with "session", you just need to include that in your shiny server function signature (i.e. function(input, output, session) ).
